title: The board’s votes on these contracts, from its official minutes, against the dates the papers give for the work
question: Did the Board of Education actually vote on these contracts, when, and had the work begun before that vote?
finding: The official minutes of 27 meetings were saved (29 files); 53 of the 115 action items fall on those meetings. 49 were adopted that night: 3 on a recorded vote of their own, the rest with the consent calendar, none with a nay recorded. No item among them was pulled, continued or voted down, so the vote date is the meeting date. For 4 (2024-06-25) the minutes list the item on the consent calendar but record no adoption of it before adjournment. Set against the vote date, 18 of the 19 adopted items that give a date for the work or the processing put it before the vote (median 45 days, at most 223); 25 of the 54 first contracts posted with them state a start before the vote (median 41 days); 12 of 12 papers with a typed signature date carry one before the vote, and the board-date line is blank in 9 of the 10 signature blocks read.
how: pdftotext -layout of each minutes PDF (official minutes attached to later “Approval of Board Minutes” items; one draft, for 8 April 2025). A separate action item is adopted where a sentence after its resolution number or vendor name reads “was moved by Commissioner … adopted by N ayes”. A consent item is placed by its subject’s opening words (or its vendor’s name inside the consent listing) and takes the first consent-calendar adoption sentence after it, so a retroactive or sole-source calendar adopted on its own line gets that line. Vote date = the meeting date. The puller’s vote column (the “contracts by meeting” table) agrees on every item it covers.
limits: Minutes for 2 meetings with action items here were sought and not obtained (2021-05-25: the minutes item holds only a link to a private mail attachment; 2022-12-08: no minutes published for the special budget-training meeting), and the other meetings in the table were not sought, so most list items have no recorded outcome on disk. A consent vote is one motion for the whole calendar: it shows the board approved the item, not that it discussed it. Some minutes say an item was severed, withdrawn, corrected or excepted without naming these items; the puller and the owner checked the item numbers. Three minutes (2018-2019) are scans read by OCR. Roll-call names are given only for absences, abstentions and recusals. A vote after the work began is what a ratification or retroactive item asks for, and the papers say so.
